# Mavuno walkthrough rerun — 2026-10-02

Status: **incomplete; no provider Mavuno journey captured**. Pilot preparation is saved separately; P2-07 and P4-04 remain open.

## Environment and scope

- Tested checkout: `aec6e07` (pilot documentation), with runtime changes through `ba37fc4`.
- Node 24.18.0; isolated Redis 7 Alpine container and a fresh demo key prefix.
- Shared sandbox service alias: `mavuno-test-channel`; disposable simulator callers only.
- Response budget: default 160 bytes for the entire UTF-8 response, including CON/END.
- The owner requested TryCloudflare and explicitly approved disposable simulator phone/session IDs and synthetic choices passing through Cloudflare. No credentials or production/customer data were used.
- A temporary loopback ingress exposes only GET `/ready` and POST `/africas-talking/ussd`; other routes return 404. The event URL remains N/A, and no authenticated provider event delivery was configured or tested.

## Independent local/public controls

- All 45 Redis/HTTP integration checks passed, with open-handle detection.
- Installed-tarball Mavuno validation passed: browser/provider-shaped synthetic order placement, receipt replay, local end-event acknowledgement, asynchronous callback lookup, cancellation and restored stock. These are synthetic controls, not actual provider traffic.
- Local readiness returned 200. Synthetic callback returned 200, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, and a 56-byte CON main menu. An exact callback repeat returned the same response.
- Public TryCloudflare readiness and synthetic callback returned the same successful statuses/menu. A public request to `/` returned 404, verifying the route restriction.
- Public readiness still returned 200 during the simulator connection attempts (checks through 07:17 UTC / 10:17 EAT).

## Provider and UI observations

- The sandbox channel previously pointed at a stopped tunnel. Its callback was changed to the new reachable tunnel and saved. A full dashboard reload showed the exact new callback URL. This is configuration read-back, not proof of provider routing.
- The simulator initially used its default country prefix. It reached the handset home screen before any dial; no Mavuno callback was generated by that connection. The caller format was corrected to a full Kenyan disposable demo number before a USSD attempt.
- Two fresh Kenyan disposable caller connection attempts remained on `Connecting...`, each observed for more than a minute. Neither reached the keypad/dial stage. No actual initial USSD callback, order, new-session lookup or cancellation was observed.
- The callback log contained three synthetic controls and zero other callbacks at the independent count check at 07:12:56 UTC. Subsequent public readiness checks remained successful.
- Brave's active window/tab changed to unrelated content during later control actions, and the computer-use tool rejected stale-context actions. Uninterrupted simulator access was requested before a final keyboard-entry attempt; that attempt has not been completed.
- The provider's [status page](https://status.africastalking.com/) listed Sandbox and USSD operational when checked during this run. That does not diagnose an individual browser/simulator connection.

## Interpretation and remaining gate

There is no evidence of an application callback failure in this run: the provider journey never got as far as a dial. Public ingress and synthetic application controls passed. The simulator connection root cause is unknown; browser/form behavior, transport and provider-side connection state were not independently distinguished. Do not infer a service outage from the spinner or count synthetic controls as provider proof.

Continue only after uninterrupted simulator access is available. Verify connection with the intended disposable caller, dial the provisioned service, cross-check a fresh provider session detail against the exact active tunnel, then perform the full order/replay/new-session/cancellation/back/validation/abandonment journey. Check end-event compatibility separately. The temporary host must be revalidated before every continuation; a saved callback URL alone does not establish that its tunnel is alive.

Raw phone numbers, provider session IDs, temporary hostname, credentials and business identifiers are omitted. Temporary local service/tunnel state must be checked independently at continuation; it is not durable deployment evidence.
